cues: Welcome to Claude Cowork — the complete visual guide.
Prepared by Sara Salem.
In this video, you'll discover every type of work Claude Cowork can do for you, and learn how to build a real task with it — step by step, from setup to a finished, scheduled workflow.
Let's start with a simple comparison.
In a normal chat, Claude answers your question. But you still gather the files, copy the content, build the documents, and repeat the work every week — yourself.

Claude Cowork is different. It's Claude's agentic mode for everyday knowledge work. It reads the files in a folder you choose, plans the task, does the work across many steps, and delivers finished files — while you stay in control.
In short: chat gives you answers. Cowork gets the work done with you.
So, what exactly is Claude Cowork?
Claude Cowork lives in the Claude desktop app. It brings the same agent power behind Claude Code to everyone — no coding needed.
It works with your files — reading, organizing, and creating documents in the folders you share.
It connects to your tools — like Google Drive, Slack, and your email — through connectors and plugins.
And it delivers real results — reports, spreadsheets, and presentations, ready to use.
At its core, Cowork works in a loop.
First, it understands the task — reading your request and the files you shared.
Then it makes a plan — breaking big work into clear steps, and sometimes splitting it across sub-agents working in parallel.
Next, it does the work — reading, writing, and building your files.
And finally, it checks and delivers the result, and shows you its progress along the way. Then it repeats, until the job is done.
Now, let's look at all the types of work you can hand to Cowork.
Files and documents. Organize a messy folder, rename files, or turn rough notes into a polished Word report.
Research. Read many sources and documents, then write a clear summary with the key findings.
Data and spreadsheets. Clean up data, build Excel models with working formulas, and create charts.
Presentations. Turn a document or an outline into a complete slide deck.
Browser tasks. Paired with Claude in Chrome, Cowork can work on websites — filling forms and collecting information.
And scheduled tasks. Recurring work — like a daily briefing or a weekly report — that runs automatically, on a schedule.
Before we build, there are four building blocks you need to know.
Folder access. Cowork only works inside the folders you choose to share — nothing else.
Connectors. They link Claude to your apps and data, like Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, and Notion.
Skills. Packaged know-how that teaches Claude how to do a task well — like creating Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files.
And plugins. Ready-made bundles of skills, connectors, and commands for a role — like sales, finance, or marketing.
Now let's build a real task, step by step. Step one: set up Cowork.
First, download and install the Claude desktop app, for Mac or Windows.
Sign in with your Claude account. Cowork is available on paid plans.
Open the Cowork tab, to switch from chat to Cowork.
Then choose a working folder — for example, the folder with your sales data. Claude can only see what's inside it.
Step two: write a clear task brief.
Start with the goal — what you want, in one line. Here, it's a quarterly sales report.
Then list the inputs — which files to read, and which template to follow.
Describe the output exactly — the file types, the sections, and the charts you expect.
And add your rules — like asking before deleting or overwriting anything. A clear brief is the secret to great results.
Step three: connect your tools.
Layer one is your local folder — the files on your computer that you choose to share.
Layer two is connectors — so Claude can read from and write to your apps, like Google Drive, Gmail, and Slack.
Layer three is the browser — with Claude in Chrome, Cowork can also work on websites for you.
Tip: connect only the tools this task needs. Fewer tools means a safer, more focused task.
Step four: run the task.
Here's our request: turn the sales files into a quarterly report.
First, Cowork reads every file in the folder, to understand the data.
Then it shares a plan, so you can see exactly what it will do.
Next, it splits the work — sub-agents can handle different parts at the same time.
Then it builds the files — a Word report with charts, and an Excel workbook with the totals. And finally it delivers them to your folder, with a short summary of what it did.
Step five: review and refine.
Open the files and check the result. Then give feedback, just like you would to a colleague — Cowork updates the work.
Watch how the quality improves with every round of feedback. In this example, the report goes from a first draft to a finished result in a few rounds.
Two files delivered, three rounds of feedback, and zero open issues at the end.
Remember: you are the reviewer. Always check numbers and facts before you share the work.
Step six: add skills.
The Word skill creates professional documents — with headings, tables, and a clean layout.
The Excel skill builds spreadsheets with real, working formulas and charts.
The PowerPoint skill turns your content into complete, well-designed slide decks.
And you can create your own custom skills — to teach Claude your team's way of working, and reuse it every time.
Step seven: install a plugin for your role.
Open the plugin directory, and browse plugins built for different jobs — like finance, sales, marketing, and legal.
Each plugin bundles skills, connectors, and slash commands for that role.
Install one, and its skills appear right away — you can run them with a slash command.
For example, a finance plugin can help with reconciliations and journal entries. Teams can also build and share their own private plugins.
Step eight: schedule it, so it runs automatically.
A one-time task runs once, when you start it. Great for new or one-off work.
A scheduled task runs on a schedule — daily, weekly, or on demand — using the same connectors, skills, and plugins.
Create one with the schedule command, or from the Scheduled section in the sidebar.
Remember: scheduled tasks run on your computer, so keep it awake and the Claude app open.
Step nine: stay safe and in control.
Share only the folder the task needs. Review the plan before Claude starts. And approve before anything is deleted.
Watch the progress, and stop the task at any time. Keep backups of important files.
Use only connectors you trust. And be careful with untrusted websites — they can contain hidden instructions. Cowork is powerful, so stay in the loop.
Here are six best practices for Claude Cowork.
One: write a clear brief — the goal, the inputs, and the exact output.
Two: share one focused folder, with only the files the task needs.
Three: start small. Test a task once before you schedule it.
Four: use skills and plugins, so you get the best results for each type of work.
Five: always review the output before you share it.
And six: turn repeat work into scheduled tasks — and save hours every week.
So, Claude Cowork in one line: brief, delegate, review. Claude does the work across your files and tools — and you stay in control.
From one-time tasks to scheduled workflows, Cowork turns hours of busywork into finished results.
Thank you for watching this complete guide to Claude Cowork.
